claims.text: 8-week once-daily empiric PPI trial before a meal for classic GERD without alarm symptoms
claims.quote: we recommend an 8-week trial of empiric proton pump inhibitor (PPI) once daily before a meal.

claims.text: Attempt to discontinue PPIs if symptoms respond to the 8-week trial
claims.quote: We recommend attempting to discontinue the PPIs in patients whose classic GERD symptoms respond to an 8-week empiric trial of PPIs.

claims.text: GERD among the most common conditions seen by gastroenterologists, surgeons and primary care physicians
claims.quote: continues to be among the most common diseases seen by gastroenterologists, surgeons, and primary care physicians

claims.text: GERD symptoms nonspecific and overlap with EoE, achalasia, functional disorders, cardiac or lung disease
claims.quote: The symptoms of GERD are nonspecific and may overlap or be confused with those of other disorders such as rumination, achalasia, eosinophilic esophagitis, reflux hypersensitivity, functional disease, cardiac or pulmonary disease

claims.text: GERD definition and objective confirmation by endoscopy and/or reflux monitoring
claims.quote: GERD is objectively defined by the presence of characteristic mucosal injury seen at endoscopy and/or abnormal esophageal acid exposure demonstrated on a reflux monitoring study.

claims.text: GERD definition: reflux of gastric contents causing symptoms and/or complications
claims.quote: GERD is the condition in which the reflux of gastric contents into the esophagus results in symptoms and/or complications.

claims.text: Transient LES relaxations enable reflux episodes
claims.quote: reduces the transient LES relaxations that enable reflux episodes.

claims.text: Alcohol, smoking, chocolate, peppermint, high-fat foods reduce LES pressure in lab studies
claims.quote: Alcohol consumption, tobacco smoking, chocolate, peppermint, and high-fat foods do reduce LES pressure in the laboratory

claims.text: Obesity increases GERD risk, possibly via intra-abdominal pressure
claims.quote: Obesity increases the risk of GERD, possibly due to a combination of eating a diet high in fat and other foods that promote reflux, increased intra-abdominal pressure

claims.text: Functional heartburn patients unlikely to respond to PPIs
claims.quote: There are likely many patients included in NERD who have functional heartburn and thus unlikely to respond to PPI.

claims.text: EoE is a diagnostic consideration when symptoms do not resolve on PPIs
claims.quote: eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE), which is a diagnostic consideration when endoscopy is performed for patients with symptoms that are thought to be due to GERD but are not eliminated by PPIs

claims.text: ACG recommends against routinely adding medical therapies in PPI non-responders
claims.quote: We recommend against routine addition of medical therapies in PPI non-responders.

claims.text: Heartburn and regurgitation definitions
claims.quote: Heartburn is the most common GERD symptom, and is described as substernal burning sensation rising from the epigastrium up toward the neck. Regurgitation is the effortless return of gastric contents upward toward the mouth

claims.text: Eating within 3 hours of lying down associated with more symptoms and medication need
claims.quote: A short interval (<3 hours) between eating and bedtime or lying supine is associated with increased GERD symptoms and need for medication

claims.text: Extraesophageal symptoms attributed to reflux are nonspecific and overlap with other disorders
claims.quote: including chronic cough, throat-clearing, hoarseness, globus, asthma, and laryngitis. These are vexing for patients as well as physicians, as the symptoms ascribed to extra-esophageal GERD are often non-specific and overlap with other disorders.

claims.text: Endoscopy first for dysphagia or other alarm symptoms (weight loss, GI bleeding) and multiple Barrett risk factors
claims.quote: We recommend endoscopy as the first test for evaluation of patients presenting with dysphagia or other alarm symptoms (weight loss, GI bleeding), and for patients with multiple risk factors for Barrett’s esophagus.

claims.text: Alarm symptoms include vomiting and anemia; endoscopy as soon as feasible
claims.quote: For patients with GERD symptoms who also have alarm symptoms such as dysphagia, weight loss, bleeding, vomiting, and/or anemia, endoscopy should be performed as soon as feasible.

claims.text: On-demand or intermittent PPI suggested for NERD heartburn control
claims.quote: We suggest on-demand or intermittent PPI therapy for heartburn symptom control in patients with non-erosive reflux disease.

claims.text: LA grade C or D: indefinite maintenance PPI or antireflux surgery
claims.quote: We recommend maintenance PPI therapy indefinitely or antireflux surgery for patients with Los Angeles grade C or D esophagitis.

claims.text: Maintenance PPI for severe EE and Barrett esophagus
claims.quote: Maintenance PPI therapy should be administered for patients with GERD complications including severe erosive esophagitis (LA C or D) and Barrett’s esophagus

claims.text: Maintenance at lowest effective dose
claims.quote: the PPIs should be administered in the lowest dose that effectively controls GERD symptoms and maintains healing of reflux esophagitis.

claims.text: Optimization of PPI therapy is first step for refractory GERD
claims.quote: We recommend optimization of PPI therapy as the first step in management of refractory GERD.

claims.text: PPI 30-60 minutes before a meal rather than at bedtime
claims.quote: We recommend PPI administration 30 to 60 minutes prior to a meal rather than at bedtime for GERD symptom control.

claims.text: Veterans trial: 11.4% improved by half or more with optimized omeprazole dosing
claims.quote: 42 of 366 (11.4%) participants had ≥50% improvement in GERD symptoms when omeprazole use was optimized

claims.text: Small but clinically significant number improve with optimization
claims.quote: a small, but clinically significant number of patients will have symptom improvement with the simple, low-cost intervention of optimizing PPI therapy.

claims.text: PPIs most effective medical treatment for GERD
claims.quote: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are the most effective medical treatment for gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).

claims.text: PPI over H2RA for healing EE
claims.quote: We recommend treatment with PPI over treatment with H2RA for healing erosive esophagitis.

claims.text: PPI over H2RA for maintenance of healing EE
claims.quote: We recommend treatment with PPI over H2RA for maintenance of healing from erosive esophagitis.

claims.text: Symptom relief and healing differ little among PPIs
claims.quote: Meta-analyses suggest that overall GERD symptom relief and healing rates differ little among the seven available PPIs

claims.text: More than one PPI switch cannot be supported
claims.quote: For patients who have not responded to one PPI, more than one switch to another PPI cannot be supported.

claims.text: Step-down to H2RA acceptable, particularly NERD
claims.quote: Step-down therapy to HRAs is another acceptable option for management, particularly in NERD patients

claims.text: Bedtime H2RA tachyphylaxis after a month; as-needed use
claims.quote: a well-done study demonstrated loss of pH control (tachyphylaxis) after a month of bedtime HRA therapy

claims.text: Bedtime H2RA may be beneficial on as-needed basis
claims.quote: use of a bedtime HRA may be beneficial if dosed on an as-needed basis for patients with nocturnal symptoms

claims.text: Antacids used only for on-demand relief; little evidence favoring one type
claims.quote: Antacids are used exclusively for on-demand symptom relief with little evidence to favor one type over another.

claims.text: UK alginate preparation; variable alginate content elsewhere
claims.quote: Studies with an alginic acid preparation manufactured in the United Kingdom suggest potential efficacy in symptom relief compared to other products, but alginate content of preparations sold in other countries is variable

claims.text: Lifestyle modifications part of medical management; supporting data limited
claims.quote: Supporting data for these recommendations are limited and variable, often involving only small and uncontrolled studies

claims.text: Head-of-bed elevation or wedge improves nocturnal symptoms and acid exposure
claims.quote: several randomized controlled trials, have demonstrated improvement in nocturnal GERD symptoms and nocturnal esophageal acid exposure with head of bed elevation or sleeping on a wedge.

claims.text: Right-side recumbency increases nocturnal reflux vs left
claims.quote: compared to lying left-side down, lying right-side down increases nocturnal reflux and reflux after meals

claims.text: Suggest elevating head of bed for nighttime symptoms
claims.quote: We suggest elevating head of bed for nighttime GERD symptoms.

claims.text: Weight loss strongly recommended for overweight and obese
claims.quote: We recommend weight loss in overweight and obese patients for improvement of GERD symptoms. (Strong recommendation, moderate level of evidence)

claims.text: 40% reduction in frequent symptoms with BMI reduction of 3.5 or more in women
claims.quote: One study documented a 40% reduction in frequent GERD symptoms in women who reduced their BMI by 3.5 or more compared with controls

claims.text: Avoid meals within 2-3 hours of bedtime
claims.quote: We suggest avoiding meals within 2-3 hours of bedtime.

claims.text: Trigger foods list
claims.quote: cessation of foods that potentially aggravate reflux symptoms such as coffee, chocolate, carbonated beverages, spicy foods, acidic foods such as citrus and tomatoes, and foods with high fat content

claims.text: Suggest avoiding trigger foods
claims.quote: We suggest avoidance of "trigger foods" for GERD symptom control.

claims.text: Smoking cessation 44% vs 18% improvement
claims.quote: those who successfully quit smoking for a year had 44% improvement in GERD symptoms, compared to 18% in those who continued to smoke

claims.text: Attempt to stop or switch to on-demand PPI if no EE/BE and symptoms resolved
claims.quote: For GERD patients who do not have erosive esophagitis or Barrett’s esophagus, and whose symptoms have resolved with PPI therapy, an attempt should be made to discontinue PPIs or to switch to on-demand therapy

claims.text: On-demand PPI not better than continuous for EE
claims.quote: On-demand PPI therapy was not better than continuous PPI therapy for patients with erosive esophagitis.

claims.text: Rebound acid hypersecretion in healthy controls; strong evidence for symptom increase lacking
claims.quote: Although rebound acid hypersecretion has been demonstrated to occur in healthy controls, strong evidence for an increase in symptoms after abrupt PPI withdrawal is lacking

claims.text: Observational studies associate PPIs with fractures, CKD, infections, dementia; do not establish cause and effect
claims.quote: Those studies have flaws, are not considered definitive, and do not establish a cause-and-effect relationship between PPIs and the adverse conditions.

claims.text: High-quality studies: no significant increase except intestinal infections
claims.quote: High-quality studies have found that PPIs do not significantly increase the risk for any of these conditions except intestinal infections.

claims.text: Benefits far outweigh theoretical risks
claims.quote: For the treatment of GERD, gastroenterologists generally agree that the well-established benefits of PPIs far outweigh their theoretical risks.

claims.text: Small increase in risk cannot be excluded
claims.quote: Nevertheless, we cannot exclude the possibility that PPIs might confer a small increase in the risk of developing these adverse conditions.

claims.text: Associations in observational studies cannot establish cause-and-effect
claims.quote: the mere identification of an association between PPIs and adverse conditions in observational studies cannot establish a cause-and-effect relationship

claims.text: No calcium/vitamin D or BMD monitoring for patients without bone risk factors
claims.quote: For GERD patients on PPIs who have no other risk factors for bone disease, we do not recommend that they raise their intake of calcium or vitamin D, or that they have routine monitoring of bone mineral density.

claims.text: No routine creatinine monitoring without kidney risk factors
claims.quote: For GERD patients on PPIs who have no other risk factors for kidney disease, we do not recommend that they have routine monitoring of serum creatinine levels.

claims.text: Pantoprazole RCT 3 years: no significant differences (incl. CKD, dementia) except enteric infections 1.4% vs 1.0%
claims.quote: The investigators found no significant differences between the PPI and placebo groups in rates of occurrence for any of those potential side effects except for enteric infections (1.4% vs 1.0% in the PPI and placebo groups, respectively

claims.text: Trial outcomes included CKD and dementia, over 3 years
claims.quote: data were collected at 6-month intervals over a period of 3 years specifically with the intent of identifying potential PPI side effects including pneumonia,infection, other enteric infections, fractures, gastric atrophy, chronic kidney disease, dementia

claims.text: Gastric acid suppression allows pathogens to survive and cause enteric infections
claims.quote: gastric acid suppression can enable ingested pathogens that ordinarily would have been destroyed by gastric acid to survive and cause enteric infections

claims.text: Magnesium monitoring: AGA no routine screening, FDA consider monitoring, ACG insufficient data
claims.quote: A recent AGA Best Practice Recommendation concluded that long-term PPI users should not routinely screen or monitor serum magnesium levels [], whereas the FDA suggests that health care providers should consider monitoring magnesium levels prior to initiation of PPI treatment

claims.text: ACG: insufficient data for magnesium monitoring recommendation
claims.quote: We feel that presently there is insufficient data to make a meaningful recommendation regarding the need for monitoring of magnesium levels in patients on chronic PPI therapy.

claims.text: Suggest against LPR diagnosis on laryngoscopy alone
claims.quote: We suggest against a diagnosis of laryngopharyngeal reflux based on laryngoscopy findings alone and recommend additional testing should be considered.

claims.text: Laryngoscopy signs have low specificity, seen in asymptomatic volunteers
claims.quote: LPR signs on laryngoscopy were found to have low specificity, with validation hampered by the lack of a gold standard for diagnosis

claims.text: Evaluate non-GERD causes before ascribing extraesophageal symptoms to GERD
claims.quote: We recommend evaluation for non-GERD causes in patients with possible extra-esophageal manifestations before ascribing symptoms to GERD.

claims.text: Reflux testing before PPI when extraesophageal symptoms without typical symptoms
claims.quote: We recommend that patients who have extra-esophageal manifestations of GERD without typical GERD symptoms (e.g. heartburn, regurgitation) undergo reflux testing for evaluation prior to PPI therapy.

claims.text: Twice-daily PPI 8-12 weeks when both extraesophageal and typical symptoms
claims.quote: For patients who have both extraesophageal and typical GERD symptoms we suggest considering a trial of twice-daily PPI therapy for 8 to 12 weeks prior to additional testing.

claims.text: PPI often ineffective for extraesophageal symptoms
claims.quote: PPI treatment is relied upon as both a diagnostic tool and treatment for extraesophageal GERD symptoms, but is often ineffective

claims.text: Heartburn more likely to respond to PPIs than extraesophageal symptoms
claims.quote: Heartburn is more likely to respond to PPIs than regurgitation or extraesophageal symptoms.

claims.text: About two-thirds of pregnant women have heartburn; any trimester; resolves after delivery
claims.quote: Approximately two-thirds of pregnant women experience heartburn, which can begin in any trimester

claims.text: Heartburn usually resolves after delivery
claims.quote: heartburn usually resolves after delivery

claims.text: Pregnancy: lifestyle first; then antacids, alginates, sucralfate first-line
claims.quote: treatment of GERD during pregnancy should start with lifestyle modifications. When lifestyle modifications fail, antacids (aluminum-, calcium-, or magnesium-containing), alginates, and sucralfate are the first-line therapeutic agents.

claims.text: Sucralfate not recommended except during pregnancy
claims.quote: We do not recommend sucralfate for GERD therapy except during pregnancy.

claims.text: Sucralfate largely unabsorbed, no systemic toxicity
claims.quote: Sucralfate is largely unabsorbed and has no systemic toxicity.

claims.text: Refractory GERD definition: 8 weeks of double-dose PPI
claims.quote: The most commonly accepted definition of refractory GERD is persistent heartburn and/or regurgitation despite 8 weeks of double-dose PPI therapy

claims.text: Optimization: PPI 30-60 minutes before first meal; before dinner for twice-daily
claims.quote: confirming that the PPI is taken 30 to 60 minutes before the first meal of the day for daily dosing and before the first and dinner meal for twice daily dosing

claims.text: Bedtime dosing less effective
claims.quote: Bedtime dosing is discouraged as this is less effective than a pre-dinner dose in acid control

claims.text: Endoscopy after stopping PPIs 2-4 weeks for refractory
claims.quote: If not already performed off PPIs, we recommend diagnostic upper endoscopy after discontinuing PPI therapy, ideally for two to four weeks.

claims.text: Reflux monitoring off therapy when GERD not established
claims.quote: In patients for whom the diagnosis of GERD is suspected but not clear, and endoscopy shows no objective evidence of GERD, we recommend reflux monitoring be performed off therapy to establish the diagnosis.

claims.text: LPR not responding to twice-daily PPI: endoscopy off PPIs 2-4 weeks, reflux monitoring if normal
claims.quote: For patients whose extraesophageal symptoms have not responded to a trial of twice-daily PPIs, we recommend upper endoscopy, ideally off PPIs for 2 to 4 weeks. If endoscopy is normal, consider reflux monitoring.

claims.text: Antireflux surgery option for objective GERD
claims.quote: We recommend antireflux surgery performed by an experienced surgeon as an option for long-term treatment of patients with objective evidence of GERD

claims.text: MSA alternative to fundoplication for regurgitation failing medical management
claims.quote: We recommend consideration of magnetic sphincter augmentation (MSA) as an alternative to laparoscopic fundoplication for patients with regurgitation who fail medical management.

claims.text: ACG published its updated GERD guideline in January 2022 (PubMed record date 2022 Jan 01, vol 117 issue 1)
claims.quote: In this new document, we provide updated, evidence-based recommendations and practical guidance for the evaluation and management of GERD

claims.text: Pooled observational evidence cannot establish causation
claims.quote: The pooled evidence from observational studies (cohort and case-control studies) cannot provide an interpretation regarding causation.

claims.text: Authors: PPI therapy should not stop in GERD patients until RCTs confirm
claims.quote: Until further randomized control trials (RCTs) and biological studies confirm these results, PPI therapy should not stop patients with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).

claims.text: FDA added fracture warning to PPI labeling in 2010
claims.quote: In 2010, the US FDA revised the labeling of PPIs to include a warning about the possible increased risk of bone fractures with their use.

claims.text: Proposed mechanism: reduced calcium absorption
claims.quote: the increase in gastric pH with the use of PPIs may impede calcium absorption.

claims.text: Pantoprazole does not inhibit CYP2C19
claims.quote: Pantoprazole does not inhibit CYP2C19.

claims.text: Cohort studies associate PPI use with CKD, progression and ESRD
claims.quote: They found that PPI use was associated with a higher incidence of CKD, kidney disease progression and end-stage renal disease (ESRD).

claims.text: FDA 2011 drug safety communication on hypomagnesemia
claims.quote: In 2011, the US FDA issued a drug safety communication regarding the potential association between PPI use and hypomagnesemia.

claims.text: Medicines that lower magnesium (e.g., diuretics) raise hypomagnesemia risk
claims.quote: Patients with CKD and those receiving medications known to lower magnesium concentration, such as diuretics, are also thought to be at higher risk.

claims.text: Two large German observational studies on dementia: small effect, low-quality evidence
claims.quote: These two large observational studies show a small effect size but have a low quality of evidence.

claims.text: Avoid unnecessary long-term prescribing, especially in older adults
claims.quote: The ongoing need for PPI therapy should be closely evaluated particularly in elderly patients.

claims.text: Seek care for diarrhea that does not improve
claims.quote: Seek immediate care if you use PPIs and develop diarrhea that does not improve.

claims.text: Use lowest dose and shortest duration appropriate to the condition
claims.quote: Patients should use the lowest dose and shortest duration of PPI therapy appropriate to the condition being treated.

claims.text: Barrett: columnar epithelium with goblet cells replacing squamous; associated with chronic GERD
claims.quote: the normal squamous epithelium is replaced by specialized columnar epithelium with goblet cells (). This metaplastic change is associated with chronic gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)

claims.text: Only known precursor of esophageal adenocarcinoma
claims.quote: BE is the only known precursor lesion of esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC)

claims.text: Annual progression 0.05%-0.2% NDBE, about 0.7% LGD
claims.quote: The annual incidence of cancer progression in BE is estimated at 0.2%–0.05% per year for NDBE and approximately 0.7% per year for LGD

claims.text: Single screening endoscopy for chronic GERD plus 3 or more risk factors (male, >50, White, smoking, obesity, family history)
claims.quote: We suggest a single screening endoscopy for patients with chronic GERD symptoms and 3 or more additional risk factors for BE, including male sex, age >50 years, White race, tobacco smoking, obesity, and family history of BE or EAC

claims.text: Chronic reflux symptoms defined as weekly for 5 or more years
claims.quote: chronic reflux symptoms (defined as weekly symptoms for 5 or more years)

claims.text: NDBE surveillance: >=3 cm every 3 years, <3 cm every 5 years
claims.quote: longer segments of BE (≥3 cm) are surveyed on a 3-year interval and shorter segments of BE (<3 cm) are surveyed on a 5-year interval

claims.text: LGD surveillance every 6 months for 1 year then annually
claims.quote: In patients with LGD undergoing surveillance, we suggest that surveillance should be performed at 6-month intervals for 1 year and then annually

claims.text: EET recommended for HGD and LGD
claims.quote: We recommend endoscopic eradication therapy for patients with BE and high-grade dysplasia and those with BE and low-grade dysplasia.

claims.text: RFA preferred ablative technique
claims.quote: Among patients undergoing EET, RFA is the preferred ablative technique.

claims.quote: Throat clearing.

claims.text: Hoarseness

claims.text: Postnasal drip
claims.quote: Postnasal drip.

claims.text: Chronic sore throat

claims.text: Laryngitis
claims.quote: Laryngitis (inflammation of your vocal cords or losing your voice).

claims.text: Often no heartburn

claims.quote: Eat dinner earlier. Try not to recline or lie down for three hours after eating.

claims.text: Avoid drying substances such as caffeine and alcohol
claims.quote: avoid drying substances, like caffeine, alcohol and menthol cough drops.
